The issue in the code is that it calculates the absolute value of the sum of the scores of persons 1 to N-1, which is incorrect. The final score of person N should be the negative of this sum, as the sum of all scores in the game must be zero.

Here is the patch to fix the issue:

# modification 1
```
<file>faultyVersion.java</file>
<original>
		System.out.println(Math.abs((int)sum)); // faultLocation.txt identifies this line as the provided fault location. It is used because Ochiai fault localization is unavailable.
</original>
<patched>
		System.out.println(-sum); // faultLocation.txt identifies this line as the provided fault location. It is used because Ochiai fault localization is unavailable.
</patched>
```

Explanation:
- The original code incorrectly takes the absolute value of the sum of the scores of persons 1 to N-1.
- The correct approach is to print the negative of this sum, as the sum of all scores must be zero, and thus the score of person N is the negative of the sum of the scores of persons 1 to N-1.
